verdict_reason: Repaired and verified. direction_norm names the FINAL layer's mean-difference norm, but zero-direction layers were dropped with `continue` and the headline was taken from the last SURVIVING entry -- so when the final layer's class means coincided, an earlier block's numbers were published under the final layer's name. A zero direction is an answer: the released get_mean_diff returns the zero vector there. Verified through the real evaluate() by making the final block's output class-independent but sample-varied (patched at module level, because the task re-reads that block through a forward hook that would overwrite anything injected into hidden_states): the repaired task reports direction_norm exactly 0.0 with separability_auc NaN, where the pre-repair code published an earlier block's norm (0.0425 on gpt2, 0.0471 on llama). 4 executed parity assertions against the official difference-of-means kernel pass.
comparable_reason: auc_at_depth_100, best_layer_separability_auc and separability_auc were all 0.8125 on a gpt2 run -- three bit-identical public columns, because on that model the best layer IS the last. They are not collinear by construction, but they will be whenever the argmax lands on the final layer.
github_reason: tests/tasks/parity/test_repe_refusal_direction_parity.py (4 assertions) against the official difference-of-means reading vector; zero-direction behaviour pinned by tests/tasks/test_refusal_direction_zero_final.py.
confounds_reason: Depth normalisation was also repaired: the depth denominator is now the deepest CANDIDATE layer index rather than the deepest index with a finite AUC, so dropping a degenerate deep layer can no longer promote an earlier block to depth 100%.
